title: Normalization projective components
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a projective $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-kun-projective]. Let $N\to C$ be the normalization, meaning the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the reduced irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Then $N\to C$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $N$ is projective and proper over $k$, and $N=\coprod_{i\in I}N_i$ for a finite set $I$, where each $N_i$ is nonempty, normal (every local ring is an integrally closed domain), integral and both open and closed in $N$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion]. Each $N_i$ is projective and proper over $k$. If $\dim C\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then $\dim N_i\le1$ for all $i$. The map $N\to C$ factors through $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ as its normalization. The set $I$ is empty if and only if $C$ is empty.

proof.text: The canonical source instance IsHProjective.isProper makes p proper, hence quasi-compact and locally of finite type. QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace and LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian make C Noetherian. Its irreducible components form a finite subtype by finite_irreducibleComponents_of_isNoetherian. The injection in hindex transfers finiteness to I.

Each a_i is a closed immersion, hence finite and locally of finite type. Its composite with p is locally of finite type. Apply Scheme.isFinite_fromNormalization_of_locallyOfFiniteType to this composite; Scheme.surjective_fromNormalization gives surjectivity. Composition makes each normalized component map to C finite.

The unique isomorphism e from the standard coproduct of the normalizations to N carries each standard coprojection to the given iota_i. The equation hnu and coproduct hom-ext identify nu with e.inv followed by the standard copairing. The source-library theorem IsFinite.sigmaDesc proves this copairing finite for every finite index type, including the empty type. Every x of C belongs to its irreducible component; hindex supplies i and z in Z_i above x. Surjectivity of the normalization supplies a point above z, whose image under iota_i lies over x.

Apply finite_over_projective_affineLocally over Spec k to nu and separately to every normalized component map to C. Its affine-base conclusion supplies IsProjective for each structure map, hence IsHProjective and IsProper by the canonical source instances.

Mathlib already makes the relative normalization of an integral source integral; apply this to the generic-point spectrum. For normal local rings, use the proved source theorem Scheme.Hom.isIntegrallyClosed_stalk_normalization, with Scheme.isIntegrallyClosed_stalk_Spec applied to the function field. These APIs implement integral closure normality and localization normality, so no new affine-chart argument is needed. Integral schemes have nonempty underlying spaces and domain stalks. Transport the open standard coprojections across e. For closedness, compose sigmaMk with the homeomorphism underlying e; Sigma.mk has closed image and this identifies its composite with iota_i.

The proved source lemma IdealSheafData.le_ker_iff_range_subset_support applies because each Z_i is reduced. The nilradical has full support, so C.nilradical is contained in the kernel of a_i. The Mathlib closed-immersion lift therefore constructs b_i to the reduction; lift_fac proves its composite is a_i. Define nured by the given coproduct colimit from the maps fromNormalization followed by b_i. Its component equations are the colimit factorization equations, and colimit hom-ext proves nured followed by the reduction immersion equals nu.

Scheme.topologicalKrullDim_normalization identifies each normalized component dimension with that of Z_i. The closed embedding a_i is inducing, and IsInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le bounds this dimension by that of C. Transitivity gives the bound by one. If I is empty, the component-cover argument above makes C empty. Conversely, a point of any integral Z_i would map to a point of C, so empty C forces empty I.

lean.statement: theorem normalization_projective_components {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (p : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsHProjective p] {I : Type u} (Z : I → Scheme.{u}) [∀ i : I, IsIntegral (Z i)] (a : ∀ i : I, Z i ⟶ C) [∀ i : I, IsClosedImmersion (a i)] (hcomponents : ∀ i : I, Set.range (a i) ∈ irreducibleComponents C) (hindex : Function.Bijective (fun i : I ↦ (⟨Set.range (a i), hcomponents i⟩ : irreducibleComponents C))) (N : Scheme.{u}) (ι : ∀ i : I, (Z i).normalization ⟶ N) (hN : IsColimit (Cofan.mk N ι)) (ν : N ⟶ C) (hν : ∀ i : I, ι i ≫ ν = (Z i).fromNormalization ≫ a i) : Finite I ∧ IsFinite ν ∧ Surjective ν ∧ IsHProjective (ν ≫ p) ∧ IsProper (ν ≫ p) ∧ (∀ i : I, Nonempty (Z i).normalization ∧ (∀ x : (Z i).normalization, IsDomain ((Z i).normalization.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed ((Z i).normalization.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ IsIntegral (Z i).normalization ∧ IsOpenImmersion (ι i) ∧ IsClosed (Set.range (ι i)) ∧ IsHProjective ((Z i).fromNormalization ≫ a i ≫ p) ∧ IsProper ((Z i).fromNormalization ≫ a i ≫ p)) ∧ (topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 1 → ∀ i : I, topologicalKrullDim (Z i).normalization ≤ 1) ∧ (∃ (b : ∀ i : I, Z i ⟶ C.nilradical.subscheme) (νred : N ⟶ C.nilradical.subscheme), (∀ i : I, b i ≫ C.nilradical.subschemeι = a i) ∧ νred ≫ C.nilradical.subschemeι = ν ∧ ∀ i : I, ι i ≫ νred = (Z i).fromNormalization ≫ b i) ∧ (IsEmpty I ↔ IsEmpty C)
